Below that: one paragraph beginning with a large woodcut initial O, running to the foot. Bottom: signature "A" at left, catchword "consensu" at right. No margin notes.

p.i: Origo Sectæ Sociniane, à Lalio Socino; & Fausto illius ex fratre nepote; quorum Historia brevi percurritur. Utriusque ingenium, eruditio, & mores, præsertim Fausti. Quomodo, & unde hic Faustus Hæresium & Hæreticorum farraginem in unum compegerit, novamque sectam de suo instituerit. Artes quibus usus est, in Dogmatibus suis uniusque ingenio commendandis, Discipulisque sibi colligendis. Opportunitates item, quas sedulo Idem arripuit, ad Hæreses suas disseminandas, præsertim in Polonia. Ejusdem superbia summa, & arrogantia, dum suo ipsius ingenio in omnibus fidit; & Amicorum Judicia vilipendit; neque hoc contentus, Catholicam Ecclesiam contemnit; eamque non suæ solius ætatis, sed & seculi Primitivi, cum Patribus, Conciliis, & unanimi

page.notes: Top right corner shows faint mirrored text ("De Socino ..."), which is show-through from the other side and was left out. The page number at top centre is in brackets; the final digit is uncertain, so it is marked [?]. The initial O is a woodcut; its word is joined as "Origo". "Lalio" and "uniusque" are read from a small, heavy print and may be imprecise. The line "uniustujusque" in the scan appears to be a printing or ligature artefact; I read it as "uniusque".
